what: The budget section gives a fixed per-core L1 of 1499136 B (a WH figure) and says the check is the sum of CB sizes against it. In fact statically allocated CBs start at the L1 allocator base (112576 B on BH: reserved region plus the 70688 B kernel-config ring), and the error compares the CB end address against max L1 (1572864 on BH). No doc names the correct runtime query, so the planner used ttnn.get_max_worker_l1_unreserved_size(). That value includes the kernel-config ring and overstates the CB budget by 70688 B, so 6 of 9 DRAM perf cases OOMed by 9-54 KB.
suggest: State that CB space = L1 end - allocator base. Give the query ttnn.get_memory_view(device, ttnn.BufferType.L1).total_bytes_per_bank, capped at the lowest allocated block_table address to leave room for live L1 tensors such as shards. Explicitly warn that get_max_worker_l1_unreserved_size() includes the kernel-config ring and must not be used as a CB budget. Replace the hard-coded WH constant with the arch-dependent query.

what: The prompt tells the op to derive shard_fit and the core grid from input_tensor.shard_spec(). The Python ttnn.Tensor has no shard_spec() method; the spec is input_tensor.memory_config().shard_spec. The implementer followed the prompt literally, so validate() raised AttributeError on every BLOCK_SHARDED cell: 300 xfail_wrong_mode plus 12 broken sharded loose cases, and it only surfaced in the golden run.
suggest: Write input_tensor.memory_config().shard_spec (grid via .grid.bounding_box(), shape via .shape) in the prompt. Also fix the same wording in the feature_spec TARGET comment ("Read op-side from ... input_tensor.shard_spec()").
